items.summary: Rejetto HTTP File Server 3.0.0–3.2.0 derives its session-cookie signing key from the non-cryptographic Math.random() generator and leaks generator outputs to unauthenticated clients during login, letting an attacker reconstruct the key, forge an admin session, and reach RCE via the server_code feature. VulnCheck observed active exploitation of exposed instances (US, Japan) on Oct 5, 2026; the flaw was found with Anthropic's Mythos model and fixed in 3.2.1.

Fortinet FortiMail (FG-IR-26-175) combines a path traversal flaw with improper NULL-byte neutralization, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker write arbitrary files via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests. Fortinet confirmed zero-day exploitation in the wild with real intrusion IOCs (ld.so.preload implants, backdoor binaries); CISA added it to KEV on Oct 1, 2026 with a federal remediation deadline of Oct 4.

Ahsay AhsayCBS up to 10.3.2 has an unauthenticated OS command injection in the Replication Receiver's /rps/api/json/UpdateReceivers.do endpoint via the 'random' argument, enabling full remote compromise. A public PoC is available; the vendor fixed it in 10.3.4. Disclosed Oct 4, 2026.

ZITADEL 3.0.0–3.4.15 and 4.0.0 before 4.17.3 links user accounts to external identity providers without verifying a primary factor or the caller's permission, so an unauthenticated attacker who knows a victim's login name can bind their own IdP identity and sign in as the victim. Part of ZITADEL's Oct 4, 2026 authentication-bypass cluster.

ZITADEL before 3.4.14 and 4.x before 4.16.2 has an authentication bypass in the hosted Login V1 UI: the 'external account not found' registration endpoint trusts client-supplied external identity fields without a completed IdP callback, enabling unauthenticated account pre-hijacking. Disclosed Oct 4, 2026.
